human_approvals.note: Two distinct things, previously presented as one and so reading as contradictory. DECISION RULINGS were given by the owner in-session, each in response to an explicit question naming the alternatives; they authorize the decisions the ADRs record. ROLE-SCOPED SIGN-OFFS are reviews of the resulting artifacts and NONE have been performed. The owner holds every role per docs/00-meta/authority-index.md, so both statements are true at once — but they are not interchangeable, and a ruling on a question is not a review of a diff.

Review findings M10 (Flutter/Dart analysis) and app/pubspec.lock are NOT done. pubspec.lock is BLOCKED, not deferred: Flutter is not installed in the build environment and a hand-written lockfile would be a fabrication.

CI caching is deferred to P1-11 but is more than cosmetic: an uncached ~32-minute Windows job that any push cancels is a merge gate that is hard to observe passing. It was cancelled 9 times in 10 runs before the branch was frozen deliberately.

The grid-alpha-opus5 environment presets a stale DATABASE_URL and SQLX_OFFLINE that are baked into the running process and cannot be changed mid-session; commands override them explicitly. CI is unaffected -- NOT because runners set nothing (the workflow does set DATABASE_URL at env: scope for every job) but because the value it sets is the correct one. An earlier revision gave the wrong reason (review finding 'minor 3').
The justfile and scripts/verify.sh remain duplicate implementations; unification is barred by D5, so drift is guarded by check-verify-parity.sh instead.
Cargo.toml, ai-toolchain.lock, rust-toolchain.toml and justfile retain CRLF. They parse correctly; repo-wide normalization is deferred to P1-11 (ADR-004).
No fixtures are delivered. alpha-spec.md 9.5 lists them under P1-00; deferred to P1-03/P1-04 and recorded in ADR-001 rather than accepted silently.

An evidence manifest structurally cannot record the SHA of its own commit. This one attests to 18c8fb72b2e7, the branch head at generation time; the commit carrying the manifest follows it and is not self-covered. CI is authoritative on the true final commit (12.8).
